title: नौवीं पहली रात
status: Gate 3 passed (D-021): all 47 pngs in content/series1/refs/ are the reference set for Phase 4. Character and wardrobe locks rewritten from the approved sheets (D-013 rule 4); style_frame set.
governed_by: docs/decisions.md D-003, D-005, D-007, D-008, D-013, D-021 (decisions govern over the bible)
look: Photoreal, cinematic, fictional Indian cast, in the photoreal proof's look carried to a dry late-April night in a small central-Indian city. Locked-room con thriller in close-ups: warm lamp against cold streetlight; branch A becomes a pale daylight sting, branch B a night siege ending in grey dawn.
style_block: STYLE: Photorealistic live-action film still, a single frame from a contemporary Indian crime thriller set in a small city in central India, shot on a full-frame digital cinema camera. Vertical 9:16 portrait composition. Late April: a warm, dry night or the first hours of the next day; no rain, no wet surfaces, a little dust in the air. Real-looking fictional Indian people with natural, un-retouched skin: visible pores, fine lines, a faint sheen of heat, no beauty smoothing, no glamour make-up; every face reads its stated age and no older. Lighting is motivated and low-key, and comes only from the sources the shot's light state names (a lamp, a bare bulb, a tube light, a streetlight, headlights, dawn or daylight through a door or window); shadows fall to deep teal-black but keep detail; no studio fill, no flat even lighting, no light from nowhere. Colour grade: warm practical light (amber lamp, yellow bulb, low sun) against cool ambient light (blue-white streetlight, pre-dawn blue, dusk), teal-leaning shadows, muted mid-tone saturation; sindoor red is the strongest colour in any frame it is in; skin stays a true warm brown; blacks very slightly lifted, never crushed. Daylight scenes keep the same grade, paler and dustier, with soft contrast. Lens: spherical prime look, 35 mm for rooms and two-shots, 50 mm for mediums, 85 mm for close-ups, 100 mm macro for hand and object inserts, near f/2 with shallow depth of field, soft round bokeh, gentle halation around bare bulbs and lamps, slight natural vignette. Camera at the eye level of the person in the shot, seated or standing, steady, level horizon, no wide-angle distortion, no Dutch tilt. Fine 35 mm film grain over the whole frame. Composed for vertical video: one clear subject, the main face in the upper-middle of the frame, the bottom fifth of the frame free of faces, important hands and essential action, and nothing important within the outer 6 percent of any edge, so the frame can be slowly pushed in or panned.
negative_rules: AVOID: No text of any kind anywhere in the image: no captions, subtitles, titles, labels, shop signs or signboard lettering, number plates, phone-screen characters or icons, readable register, ledger or notebook entries, newsprint, clock or watch digits; any written or printed surface is blank or an illegible blur. No watermarks, signatures, logos, brand names, borders, frames or split panels. No police crest, badge, insignia, flag or portrait, no national flag, no government emblem, no deity image, idol or religious symbol, no real or recognisable people. No extra people beyond those named in the shot; Billu's two helpers never show a face (head cropped, turned away or in full shadow). No weapons, no blood, no wound other than Kiran's old healed scar, no nudity, no intimacy. Do not change any character's face, age, skin tone, hair, wardrobe, jewellery, henna or chooda from the reference sheet; do not add or remove glasses, bindi, sindoor, nose ring, rings, earrings, watch, chain, cap, beard or moustache. Kiran's nose ring is in her LEFT nostril and her scar is on her LEFT forearm only. Right-hand-drive car only: the steering wheel and the driver are on the right side of the car. No ceiling fan in the bedroom. No extra, missing or fused fingers, no distorted hands, no duplicated limbs. No rain, no wet streets. No illustration, anime, cartoon, 3D render, CGI gloss, HDR glow, plastic skin, beauty filter or over-saturated colour.

grade.night: Warm practicals (amber lamp about 2700 K, yellow bulb about 2400 K) against cool blue-white streetlight about 6500 K; shadows teal-black with detail; mid-tone saturation pulled down about a fifth; sindoor red and marigold are the only fully saturated colours; skin a true warm brown; blacks lifted slightly.
grade.dawn: Blue-grey ambience warming to low orange sun; low contrast; the same teal-leaning shadows.
grade.day: Branch A daylight: pale, dusty, soft contrast, fluorescent green-white against warm daylight, saturation held down; it should feel exposed rather than bright.
grade.film: Fine 35 mm grain on every frame, gentle halation round bare bulbs and lamps, slight natural vignette.

lens_look.format: Full-frame digital cinema camera, vertical 9:16, spherical primes.
lens_look.aperture: Near f/2 (f/2.8 for exteriors and daylight wides).
lens_look.camera: Eye level of the person in the shot, seated or standing; steady; level horizon; no wide-angle distortion; no Dutch tilt.
lens_look.composition: One clear subject; main face in the upper-middle; bottom fifth free of faces and key action; nothing important in the outer 6 percent.

style_frame.decided_by: D-021 decision 3 (Gate 3). Used for all of Phase 4; it is not a stand-in for an episode anchor.
style_frame.rule: Copy only the rendering, not the room, props or light.
style_frame.rendering_means: Grade, grain, lens, skin and surface texture.
style_frame.when_attached: Only on the first frame of a new scene, last in the reference list, in the scene anchor's slot (D-013 rule 2). When the scene's own plate is bedroom_bed, attach the file once.
style_frame.prompt_label: Image N is the series style frame. Match only its rendering. Do not copy its room, furniture, props or light; the light comes from the LIGHT line.
style_frame.watch_for: The bedroom's marigold garlands, the window grille, the amber lamp or the night light turning up in other settings. If wave 1's first-of-scene frames copy its room or props in more than one frame in five, drop it from those frames and give its slot to a prop sheet. If day scenes inherit its night light, bureau_front.png becomes the style frame for day scenes (D-021, would change it).

plates.bedroom_bed: From the door towards the bed and headboard. Window wall picture-RIGHT, almirah, chair and bag picture-LEFT, lamp at the left of the headboard. Use for Aditya on the bed, Kiran at the stool and tray, two-shots across the bed.

plates.bedroom_window: From the almirah towards the window. Headboard picture-LEFT, door edge picture-RIGHT, stool and tray by the window. Use for Kiran backing to the window side (s1b01 b7), headlights on the ceiling, dawn at the window.

locations.geography: Facing the headboard: window in the RIGHT wall, almirah and chair (maroon bag on it) against the LEFT wall, door behind. Lamp on the almirah side of the headboard; stool with the tray on the window side of the bed. No ceiling fan, no ceiling light.
locations.story_props_in_plate: The plates hold the maroon bag on the chair, the empty steel tray on the stool and (bedroom_door) the locked padlock, because these are the base state for most bedroom frames. The glass and paper fold are not in the plates: their position changes beat to beat and comes from the STATE line and the glass_and_fold sheet.

plates.stairwell_up: From the street door up the flight to the landing and the pale-blue door. Use for Billu at the bedroom door (s1b01 b4), Aditya coming down behind Kiran (s1a01 b6), boots on the stairs.
plates.stairwell_down: From the landing down to the street door. Use for Kiran and Billu on the landing (s1b02 b2) and the walk down at first light (s1b03 b7).

locations.geography: One straight narrow flight; pale-blue bedroom door at the top (no lock on the landing side); dark-grey iron-sheet street door at the bottom; bare bulb over the landing.

plates.lane_night: Billu's car on picture-LEFT under the one streetlight, motorbike behind it nearer camera; the house across the lane on picture-RIGHT with the lit first-floor window above its street door.

locations.geography: Car parked opposite the house. From the car, the lit window is across the lane and up.

plates.car_forward: Rear bench looking forward: driver (Billu) picture-RIGHT, front passenger (Kiran) picture-LEFT, mirror top centre. Aditya's point of view and Billu's eyes in the mirror.
plates.car_rear: Between the front seats looking back at the rear bench: Aditya's place (rear left, behind Kiran) is on picture-RIGHT.

locations.geography: Right-hand drive. Billu front right, Kiran front left, Aditya rear left behind Kiran. At the shutter Aditya gets out on the left and opens Kiran's door, so he takes her LEFT hand.

plates.bureau_front: From the shutter into the room: desk and cashbox centre back, marigold curtain behind it, mirror wall picture-LEFT, cot picture-RIGHT, mannequin back-left corner.
plates.bureau_reverse: From behind the desk towards the shutter: mirror wall picture-RIGHT, cot picture-LEFT, desk and cashbox soft in the foreground.
plates.bureau_back_room: Through the marigold curtain into the store: steel trunk with sarees, blouse rail, small mirror, back door to the alley. s1a02 b4; Mausi fitting Chhoti's blouse (s1a02 b6); Billu's exit (s1a03 b7).
plates.bureau_exterior: The grey shutter from the street, down, at 5:40 am with low sun from picture-left. s1a01 b9 (the car arrives; attach billu_car).

locations.geography: Facing in from the shutter: mirror wall with bulbs and two parlour chairs LEFT, cot RIGHT, desk at the back facing the shutter with the cashbox on it, marigold curtain behind the desk to the back room, mannequin in the back-left corner beside the curtain. D-007 direction 16: the mirror wall stays out of wide shots; never show the camera or an unplanned face in a mirror.

plates.chowki: From the constable's side of the desk: register and tumbler in the foreground, visitor's chair across the desk, bench against the pale-yellow wall behind, barred window picture-LEFT, open door to the bright yard picture-RIGHT.

locations.geography: Kiran sits across the desk facing camera; the bench and the open door are behind her, so Aditya in the doorway (s1a03 b11) is behind her on picture-right.

bedroom.beats: s1e01, s1e02, s1a01 b1 to b5, s1b01 b1 to b6
bedroom.rule: Amber bedside lamp (almirah side) as key, cool blue-white streetlight through the window grille as rim with soft bar shadows, deep teal shadows. No overhead light.
Base state plus white headlight beams from the lane sweeping across the ceiling through the grille.

bedroom.beats: s1b01 b8 (a thin warm line under the door) and from b9, when the door is open, to s1b02 b5
bedroom.rule: Base state plus warm yellow light from the bare landing bulb spilling in through the open pale-blue door, throwing long shadows across the floor towards the bed.

bedroom.beats: s1b02 b6 to b9, s1b03 b1 to b3
bedroom.rule: Lamp still on and the landing spill continues; the window has turned deep blue, so the cool rim becomes a soft blue fill and the streetlight looks weaker.
Grey dawn light through the window becomes the main light, flat and cool; the lamp is a weak warm glow; the landing bulb is a small warm point through the door.

stairwell.rule: One bare yellow bulb over the landing; the flight falls into shadow towards the street door.
The street door at the bottom stands open on grey first light, which comes up the flight cool and soft; the bulb is still on above.

lane.rule: One cool blue-white streetlight over Billu's car; the warm amber square of the bedroom window is the only warm light.
Grey first light, cool and flat; the streetlight is off; the bedroom window is a faint warm square.

car.rule: Soft blue-grey dawn through the windscreen; faces cool and low contrast.
The first sun, low and red-orange, through the car's left-side windows; it glows through Kiran's chooda.
About 5:40 am: low warm sun from picture-left raking across the grey shutter; long soft shadows; blue-grey sky.

bureau.beats: s1a01 b9 (once the shutter is up) to b11, s1a02 b1 to b9
bureau.rule: Shutter up: pale daylight from the front, fluorescent tube on (pale green-white), mirror bulbs off. Back room: bare bulb on.
Shutter down: tube light and the row of bare mirror bulbs only; warm bulbs against green-white tube; no daylight. In b7 hard white light also comes through the slats of the shutter.
The shutter goes up and flat bright daylight floods in from the front behind the khaki sleeve; tube still on.
Tube light on, mirror bulbs on; blue dusk at the half-open shutter.

chowki.rule: Flat late-morning daylight from the barred window and the open door; the yard bright.

key_props.photograph: The one image of the print (D-007 direction 15). Every insert in which its content can be read uses this asset, cropped or re-framed, never regenerated. In wider shots the print is a small creased rectangle and its content must not contradict this asset (no face, no henna, red glass bangles, scar). Owners: Aditya (shared, s1a02 until Billu lifts it in b2), Mausi (s1a02 b7 to s1a03 b2, then face down on her desk), the chowki bench (s1a03 b11); branch B: Aditya, Mausi reads it (s1b01 b10), Kiran keeps it (s1b03 b7).
key_props.chooda: Loose and stacked bangles for s1e02 b2 to b4 (three on the sheet: two ivory, one red), s1a03 b3 (bangles dropped one by one on the desk by the cashbox) and on Chhoti in s1b03 b9 and b10.
key_props.glass_and_fold: Shared: the glass has half a fold in it and is never drunk; the half-empty fold stays on the tray. Branch A: Aditya pockets the fold (s1a01 b5) and tips it out at the bureau (s1a03 b8). Branch B: two fresh folds (s1b01 b11), never opened; a fresh warm glass in s1b02 b4. s1b03 b9 and b10 use a different steel glass at the bureau (same design is acceptable).
key_props.padlock_hasp: Locked from s1e01 to s1a01 b5 (opened with the key; view 2) or to s1b01 b8 (screws torn out from outside, padlock hanging still locked; view 3). The landing side of the door shows no lock.
key_props.key_thread: Round Aditya's neck in every shot; inserts in s1e01 b3 and when it opens the padlock (s1a01 b5).
key_props.brass_set: s1e01 b4 (from the almirah), s1a01 b6 (opened for Billu), s1a01 b10 (Mausi laughs at it).
key_props.kiran_phone: On the bed with no network (overlay) and the SIM out in s1e01 b4; SIM back in s1e02 b4; on the bed on speaker between them in s1e02 b10 to b13 and s1a01 b1 / s1b01 b1. Screen content is always an overlay; when the screen must be seen, frame it dark or as a plain glow (D-013 rule 7: state its orientation in the STATE line).
key_props.aditya_phone: Photographs the ledger (s1a02 b6); face down in s1b01 b6; pocketed by Billu in s1b01 b9.
key_props.maroon_bag: On the wooden chair beside the almirah all night (in the bedroom plates). Side pocket unzipped by Aditya in s1e02 b10 (the dabba of mathri). Grey salwar-kurta in the main pocket.
key_props.notebook: Branch B only: on the sheet with the photograph (s1b01 b6), read by Mausi (b10), kept by Kiran (s1b03 b7).
key_props.key_bunch: On Mausi's LEFT hip until taken (see Mausi's continuity notes); in Kiran's hand in s1a02 b5 and b6 and held out in s1a03 b5; knotted at Kiran's LEFT hip in s1b03 b6 to b9.
key_props.cashbox_ledger: On Mausi's desk in every bureau frame (in the bureau plates, closed). Opened in s1a02 b2 and b6; the ledger carried out under a khaki arm in s1a03 b8; Mausi writes in it in s1b03 b9.
key_props.billu_car: Parked in the lane (lane_night plate), driven in s1a01 b7 to b9, starts in s1b03 b8 with Mausi in the back seat.

prompt_assembly.reference_assets: Every file in refs/prompts/ is a complete prompt. Run it verbatim with production/scripts/codex-frame.sh <refs_dir> <id> <prompt_file> [refs in the listed order]; do NOT append style_block or negative_rules. Generate in the order of `assets` below; an asset may only be run once every ref it lists exists and has passed the sheet gate.
prompt_assembly.shot_frames: Opening line 'Use your image generation tool to create ONE new vertical 9:16 image.' + reference labels by order ('Image 1 is the line-up sheet for Kiran and Aditya; Image 2 is the location plate for the bedroom seen from the door; Image 3 is ...; match them exactly') + the shot description (framing in picture terms, action, expression) + the light-state rule + the STATE block from the continuity file (D-013 rule 3) + the wardrobe_lock for every on-screen principal, verbatim, plus shape_lock for the boys or the constable if they are in frame + style_block + negative_rules.
prompt_assembly.reference_order_and_budget: At most 5. Order: (1) the people: the pair sheet for a two-shot, else the single sheet (kiran_hands for hand inserts; kiran_p3 or chhoti_final in the endings); (2) the location plate chosen by camera direction; (3) the sheet of every prop visible; (4) the scene anchor (D-013 rule 2) last. Over 5: drop the plate first when the anchor shows the same setting (D-013 rule 1), then a single sheet that the pair sheet already covers.
prompt_assembly.faces_per_frame: No more than two sheet faces in a frame until a Gate 3 frame shows three holding (D-007 direction 16). Beats with three or more principals are cut as singles and two-shots.
prompt_assembly.framing_for_motion: Raw frames are about 941x1672, upscaled to 1440x2560 by the runner and moved with slow pushes and pans. Faces and hands that matter stay off the outer 6 percent and out of the bottom fifth (subtitles).
prompt_assembly.shell_quoting: Prompts contain apostrophes (Kiran's, viewer's). Always pass a prompt file to codex-frame.sh; never paste a prompt inside single quotes.

sheet_gate.who_checks: Visual checker with a shell (D-013 rule 10), before any asset that names the sheet as a ref is generated, and again at Gate 3.
reject_and_regenerate_if: The views on one sheet do not show the same face, or a face reads more than about five years older or younger than the stated age (the proof's Tara drift).
Any view adds or drops jewellery, a bindi, sindoor, glasses, facial hair, a watch, rings or text; or the bangles are a different colour pattern from a red cuff with ivory ends.

Side errors, checked in picture terms on the front views: Kiran's nose ring not on picture-right; Aditya's parting not on picture-right or his watch not on picture-right; Mausi's keys or pallu not on picture-right; Billu's toothpick or car key not on picture-left; Chhoti's braid, phone and bangles not on picture-left, or her henna on the wrong palm.

kiran_hands: the scar on the right arm, on the palm side, along the forearm instead of across it, red or raw, or with horns pointing to the hand; henna on the backs of the hands; any view showing the scar through a complete cuff.
photograph: any henna on the bride's hand, a chooda instead of thin glass bangles, a face, an idol, or a scar that does not match kiran_hands view 3.
Chhoti (either sheet) reads as a child rather than an adult woman (D-007 direction 14). If two regenerations still read young, her look is redesigned older and taller per D-007, not shipped.

Pair sheets: the crown-height relation stated in the prompt is visibly wrong (measure: ratio of head-top heights above the shared floor line, within about 3 percent of the cm ratio), or either face departs from its single sheet.
Plates: any person, readable text, idol, ceiling fan (bedroom) or left-hand-drive car; geography mirrored against the plate prompt (for example the window on the wrong side).
sheet_gate.recrop_not_regenerate_if: The only fault is that a view enters the outer 10 percent border (D-013 rule 8): re-crop or re-pad from the .raw.png with ffmpeg and keep the take.
sheet_gate.after_the_gate: Done (S6, 26 Nov, under D-021 decision 7): every character_lock and wardrobe_lock in this file is rewritten from the approved sheet (age read, face shape, hair side, jewellery and marks in picture-side terms); see each character's locks_source. A shot prompt may not contradict its sheet.
sheet_gate.retakes: One retake per sheet as a rule (D-013 rule 11); the sheet gate may ask for a second only for a fault in the reject list, since a flawed sheet is copied into every frame.

usage_notes: Pick Kiran's sheet by period (characters.kiran.periods). Period 1 frames never attach kiran_p2 and vice versa: the sheet is the wardrobe authority.

Any frame that shows Kiran's hands or forearms close (the hook, the wrist check, the folds in her palm, the chowki desk) attaches kiran_hands. Any frame that shows the scar states it in picture terms and attaches kiran_hands or kiran_p3.
Two-shots attach the pair sheet for that pair and period instead of two single sheets (D-013 rule 5); add a single sheet only if a slot is free and the face is large in frame.

Every prop visible in a frame attaches its prop sheet (D-013 rule 1; the proof's props drifted because their sheets were never attached). Small hand props: the STATE line gives the orientation ('back of the phone to camera'), and framings that hide what cannot be controlled are preferred; inserts carry the detail (D-013 rule 7).
The boys and the constable have no sheets: copy their shape_lock into the prompt and frame them as backs, hands, boots or silhouettes only.
All readable text (time, caller name, shop name, ledger rows, the 'मौसी' caller ID) is an overlay added in assembly. Frames leave a plain, dark or blurred surface where the overlay goes.

The scene anchor (D-013 rule 2) for the first frame of a new scene is the series style frame, content/series1/refs/bedroom_bed.png (D-021; see style_frame): attached last, labelled, and copied for rendering only, not the room, props or light.
Mirrors (bureau mirror wall, rear-view mirror): state in the shot what the mirror shows; keep the mirror wall out of wides (D-007 direction 16).

Light: copy the light-state rule for the beat from light_states into every shot prompt. The bedroom's branch B states follow D-007 direction 18; the beat ranges are this file's call and the storyboard may move a boundary by one beat if it logs it.
Timing (frame-generation skill): about 55 s per sheet or plate; 47 assets is about 43 minutes of Codex time on one lane, about 22 minutes on two, before retakes.

Sheet retake round (S6, 26 Nov): every sheet and plate png is now the raw fitted inside the centre 1152x2048 box and padded to 1440x2560 with the raw's corner colour (no crop-fill). The 14 regenerated assets used their one retake (D-013 rule 11); the older takes are kept as <id>.prev1.png / .prev1.raw.png and the old prompts as prompts/<id>.prev1.txt.

Drift logged, mausi (retake stands, better than take 1): front and three-quarter views show ONE stud, picture-right, correct. The right-profile view (nose to picture-right) still shows a stud on the visible right nostril, which the lock forbids. Storyboards avoid Mausi's right profile in close shots, or the shot prompt states 'no nose stud visible on this side'. Her close views are cut as rectangular panels.

Drift logged, lane_night (retake stands): Image 2 was stairwell_down, not stairwell_up as the checker's fix said, because stairwell_up looks up the stairs and does not show the street door. Result: a dark-grey iron-sheet door with a black latch, no shutter on the house, no hanging lamp in the window. The grille is vertical bars with one horizontal mid-rail; the door has a centre seam and may read as two leaves; the neighbour's roll-down shutter shows at the right edge.

Drift logged, kiran_p3 (retake stands): the scar is now in the lower third of the left forearm, about a quarter of the forearm's length above the wrist, still slightly higher than in kiran_hands view 3. kiran_hands stays the authority for the scar's place.

Drift logged, pair_aditya_chhoti (retake stands): the crown ratio is still about 0.87 against 0.847 expected (inside 3%); Chhoti's crown sits at Aditya's chin, not his collar. Two-shots keep her crown at his collar in the prompt. The back of her left hand is plain and her left wrist bare.

Drift logged, pair_mausi_chhoti (retake stands): all three locks fixed (plain hand backs, bare left wrist, one Mausi stud picture-right). Possible faint orange on Chhoti's right fingertips around the phone, unclear at raw resolution.
art_director_notes: Gate 3 passed (D-021). The locks in characters were rewritten from the approved sheets on 26 Nov; where a sheet differs from the bible (Aditya's chest pocket, Mausi's ring and five keys, Kiran's and Chhoti's toe-post footwear) the lock follows the sheet.

Lane light: the bible calls the lane's one streetlight sodium orange, but the bedroom's window light 'cool blue-white streetlight' and the tone line 'warm lamp against cold streetlight'. Both cannot be true of the same lamp. This file makes the lane's streetlight a cool blue-white lamp, so the bedroom's light is motivated and the only warm thing in the lane is the lit window. Flag for S1/the Arbiter if the sodium look is wanted; it would change lane_night and bedroom_night.

Chhoti follows D-007 direction 14 over the bible: 'adult woman, 19' opens her description; round cheeks, gap teeth and the ribbon are dropped; a plain white dupatta (colour chosen here) is added. Her phone is off her hand in the last scene (s1b03 b9, b10) because her hands hold the fold and the glass.

Choices the bible leaves open, set here: Mausi's nose stud on her LEFT nostril; Mausi's slippers black; the boys' trousers, shoes and Boy 2's shirt colour; Billu's car as a boxy late-1990s small sedan with blank plates; the bureau's mannequin in the back-left corner, the tube light over the curtain, a terrazzo floor and a blank pink signboard (for the name overlay); the chowki door on picture-right of the constable's view; the padlock key design.

Plates carry no one-off marks (D-013 rule 6): no stains, tears or cracks are written into any plate, and the bible's 'damp-stained' stairwell walls become 'evenly aged'. The only story marks are the torn-out hasp (a prop sheet view) and the scar (kiran_hands).
No ceiling fan in the bedroom: Mohit was found hanging from one, and the bible says his death is never pictured; a fan in the room would invite the image.

Kiran has three wardrobe sheets plus a hand sheet because each pair sheet stands in for two single sheets (D-013 rule 5) and must carry the right clothes: hence p1 and p2 versions of the Kiran-Aditya, Kiran-Mausi and Kiran-Billu pairs.

Not made: a Billu-Chhoti pair (see pairs_not_made), face sheets for the boys and the constable (bible production locks), a sheet for Mohit (he exists only in the photograph). D-005 expected about nine plates for six locations; this file has twelve, because the car needs both directions and the bureau needs its exterior and back room.
